Tom / team,

A few pragmatic storage baselines based on what we've seen work for low-latency inference at scale (keeps procurement simple):

- Hot path (embedding/generation KV & prefix cache): 1 x 2TB NVMe per inference node (preferably enterprise NVMe with sustained write spec). Mount as XFS w/ noatime; set scheduler to mq-deadline.

- Warm path (shared model artifacts and checkpoints): 4–8TB RAID1 on a small SAN per availability pod or a Rook-Ceph cluster with SSD-backed OSDs; provides snapshot/replication for model versions.

- Durable tier (backups/archives): an NFS gateway backed by object storage or a dedicated NAS; slow but cheap.

StorageClass recommendations:
- sc-hot (local-ephemeral, RWX discouraged), sc-warm (CSI — ceph-block), sc-durable (NFS/CSI for large PVCs)

PVs and eviction: set kubelet evictionHard: memory.available < 250Mi, nodefs.available < 5%, imagefs.available < 10%; for prod nodes consider node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable only during maintenance windows.

Networking/IO kernel tips: 
- disable transparent hugepages for inference containers; enable hugetlb only if you pin large-memory components.
- tcp_tw_reuse and fq_codel are fine; we avoid custom tunables unless they have validated benchmarks.

Attachments: I'm exporting our internal nodeclass guide as a PDF and a short checklist. Please find redwood-nodeclass-recommendations.pdf attached.

Kim

Adding ops/runbook perspective and rollout sequencing:

- Phase 0 (procurement & rack prep): procurement to order node SKUs per the attached spreadsheet. We need power rails (2N preferred), 10Gbps leaf uplinks, and at least one spare rack PDUs. Procurement, please confirm lead times.

- Phase 1 (staging cluster): provision a 3-node staging cluster (cpu-heavy nodeclass) using local NVMe; validate caching, model pull performance, and eviction behavior. Keep production images identical to staging.

- Phase 2 (prod canary): deploy on prod-standard cluster with 3 control-plane nodes (t3-equivalent), separate etcd nodes if you want HA beyond 3 etcd members. We recommend using a CSI-backed warm tier for model artifacts.

- Autoscaling: use ClusterAutoscaler with node groups for cpu-heavy and io-heavy. For GPU bursts, use a separate nodegroup with taint gpu=true:NoSchedule and tolerant pods.

- Monitoring/SLAs: ensure node-exporter and cAdvisor metrics stream to your PromHub; set alert for node_disk_utilization > 85% and model-cache-miss-rate > 5% (for first 30 days).

Deliverables we'll drop into the shared Drive by EOD: 1) 1-page procurement BOM, 2) 1-page preflight checklist, 3) nodeclass PDF (Kim's).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
